trick: Scan for repeats: 16 shows up three times, more than any other value.

subject: DA
q: How many sides does a polygon whose interior angles sum up to 720 degrees have?
solution: The interior angles of an n sided polygon add up to (n − 2) × 180°. So (n − 2) × 180 = 720, which gives n − 2 = 4 and n = 6. The polygon has 6 sides.

subject: DA
q: Circle graph: housing 30%, food 20%, transport 15%, other 35%. Which is the largest expense?
solution: Compare the percentages: housing 30%, food 20%, transport 15%, other 35%. The largest is 35%, which is Other. So the largest expense is Other expenses.
trick: Ignore the order they are listed in and find the biggest percentage: 35, which is Other.

subject: DA
q: Find how many standard deviations above the mean a score of 91 is if the mean = 75 and the standard deviation = 8.
solution: z = (score − mean) ÷ SD = (91 − 75) ÷ 8 = 16 ÷ 8 = 2. So the score is 2 standard deviations above the mean.
trick: 91 is 16 above 75, and 8 goes into 16 twice.

subject: DA
q: A researcher wants to test whether the population mean is lower than some hypothesized value. Which test is used?
solution: The researcher's alternative claim is that the mean is lower than the hypothesized value (μ < μ0). A claim of lower than puts the rejection region in the left tail. The answer is a Left tailed test.
trick: The direction in the claim names the tail: lower means left. The F test compares variances, so it does not fit.

subject: DA
q: A dataset has values: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. What is the 40th percentile?
showNote: The answer depends on the percentile method. Position (n + 1) × 0.4 = 2.4 gives 12, but position 1 + (n − 1) × 0.4 = 2.6, which is the NumPy default, gives 13, and both 12 and 13 are options.
solution: Use the position (n + 1) × p = 6 × 0.4 = 2.4. That is 0.4 of the way from the 2nd value (10) to the 3rd value (15). So the 40th percentile is 10 + 0.4 × 5 = 12.
trick: The position is 0.4 × 6 = 2.4, so go 40% of the way from 10 to 15. 40% of 5 is 2, which gives 12.

subject: DA
q: If the mean of a series = 120, median = 100, SD = 10, find Karl Pearson's coefficient of skewness.
solution: The mode is not given, so use Karl Pearson's median form: coefficient of skewness = 3 × (mean − median) ÷ SD = 3 × (120 − 100) ÷ 10 = 3 × 20 ÷ 10 = 6. The coefficient of skewness is 6.
trick: Mean − median is 20, and 20 ÷ 10 is 2, so times 3 gives 6.

subject: DA
q: Which of the following measurement does not divide a set of observations into equal parts?
solution: Deciles split the data into 10 equal parts and percentiles into 100 equal parts. Standard deviation is a single number that measures spread, so it does not divide the data. The answer is Standard Deviation.
trick: Deciles and percentiles are cut points. Standard deviation is a spread number and cuts nothing.

subject: DA
q: Clustering belongs to what type of data analysis?
solution: Clustering groups data points by similarity without any labels to learn from. Learning without labels is unsupervised. The answer is Unsupervised.
trick: No labels and no answers given in advance means unsupervised, and clustering has no target to predict.

subject: DA
q: How many ways can you choose 5 people from 7 men and 6 women, so that at least 3 men are on the committee?
solution: At least 3 men means 3, 4 or 5 men on the committee. 3 men and 2 women: 7C3 × 6C2 = 35 × 15 = 525; 4 men and 1 woman: 7C4 × 6C1 = 35 × 6 = 210; 5 men: 7C5 = 21. Total = 525 + 210 + 21 = 756. There are 756 ways.
trick: 7C3 and 7C4 are both 35, so add the women's ways first: 35 × (15 + 6) = 35 × 21 = 735. Then add the 21 for five men: 756.

subject: DA
q: In a team of 20 where 15 hit targets, what percentile does a target-achieving salesperson represent?
showNote: The wording is loose. A true percentile rank depends on where the person sits among the 20, so the 15 target hitters would range from about the 25th to the 95th percentile. The show just uses 15 out of 20 = 75%, and 75th is the only option that fits the numbers.
solution: 15 out of 20 hit target, and 15 ÷ 20 = 0.75, which is 75%. The question reads this share as the percentile, so the answer is the 75th percentile.
trick: Do 15 ÷ 20 = 0.75 and match it to the 75th percentile option. The other two options do not come from these numbers.

subject: DA
q: Find the skewness direction given a mean of 50 and a median of 40.
solution: The direction of skew follows the sign of (mean − median). Here 50 − 40 = 10 is positive, so the data have a positive (right) skew.
trick: Mean above median means positive skew, and mean below median means negative skew. This matches the sign of Pearson's skewness, 3 × (mean − median) ÷ SD.

subject: DA
q: An ogive shows 35% of 200 students scored below 85. How many scored above 85?
solution: An ogive shows cumulative counts, so 35% of 200 = 0.35 × 200 = 70 students scored below 85. The rest scored above, which is 200 − 70 = 130 students.
trick: If 35% are below, then 65% are above. 65% of 200 is 2 × 65 = 130.

subject: DA
q: A box contains 8 good and 4 defective bulbs. What is the probability of selecting 3 defectives?
solution: Pick 3 bulbs from 12 without replacement. P(all 3 defective) = 4/12 × 3/11 × 2/10 = 24/1320 = 1/55.
trick: Count groups instead: only 4 ways to choose 3 of the 4 defectives, and 12C3 = 12 × 11 × 10 ÷ 6 = 220 groups in all. So 4/220 = 1/55.

subject: DA
q: A store finds 15% of customers return items. In 50 sales, what's the expected number of returns?
solution: Expected returns = n × p = 50 × 0.15 = 7.5.
trick: 15% of 50 is half of 15, because 50 is half of 100. So 7.5.

subject: DA
q: The ages of 5 children in a family are: 30, 20, 10, 50, 40. What is the range of their ages?
solution: Range = largest value − smallest value = 50 − 10 = 40.
trick: Spot only the biggest (50) and the smallest (10): 50 − 10 = 40.

subject: DA
q: In a normal distribution with mean 160cm and SD of 8cm, calculate the proportion of data between 152cm and 168cm.
solution: 152 = 160 − 8 and 168 = 160 + 8, so the interval is exactly 1 standard deviation either side of the mean. About 68% of a normal distribution lies within 1 SD (68.27% to two decimals), so the proportion is 68%.
trick: Rewrite 152 and 168 as mean ± 8. That is ±1 SD, which is the 68% of the 68, 95, 99.7 rule.

subject: DA
q: A sample correlation coefficient is 0.75. What percentage of variation is explained?
solution: The share of variation explained is the coefficient of determination, r². With r = 0.75, r² = 0.75² = 0.5625, which is 56.25%.
trick: r = 3/4, so r² = 9/16 = 0.5625. You can also use 75 × 75 = 5,625 and place the decimal point.

subject: DA
q: If P(rain) = 0.4 and P(traffic) = 0.7 (assume independent), what's P(rain and traffic)?
solution: For independent events, P(rain and traffic) = P(rain) × P(traffic) = 0.4 × 0.7 = 0.28.
trick: 4 × 7 = 28, and there are two decimal places in total, so 0.28.

subject: DA
q: A student is at the 90th percentile. Out of 1,000 students, how many scored equal or lower?
solution: The 90th percentile means 90% of the scores are at or below that score. So 90% of 1,000 = 900 students scored equal or lower.
trick: Percentile means percent at or below: 90% of 1,000 is 900.

subject: DA
q: If every value in a dataset is 40, what is the standard deviation?
solution: Standard deviation measures spread around the mean. If every value is 40, the mean is 40 and every deviation is 0, so the standard deviation is 0.
trick: No spread means SD = 0. The number 40 is only a distraction.

subject: DA
q: The quartile deviation of a dataset is 8. What is the interquartile range?
solution: Quartile deviation = (Q3 − Q1) ÷ 2, and the interquartile range is Q3 − Q1. So IQR = 2 × quartile deviation = 2 × 8 = 16.
trick: The quartile deviation is half the IQR, so double it: 2 × 8 = 16.

subject: DA
q: Find the expected value for a game: win ₦200 with P = 0.3, lose ₦100 with P = 0.7
solution: Expected value = (200 × 0.3) + (−100 × 0.7) = 60 − 70 = −10. So the expected value is −₦10.
trick: Work in tens: 20 × 0.3 = 6 and 10 × 0.7 = 7, so 6 − 7 = −1 ten, which is −₦10.

subject: DA
q: A lottery has a 0.002 chance of winning. Out of 3,000 players, how many are expected to win?
solution: Expected winners = n × p = 3,000 × 0.002 = 6.
trick: 0.002 is 2 in a thousand, so 3,000 players gives 3 × 2 = 6.

subject: DA
q: If 30% of Nigerians own smartphones and you survey 250 people, expected number of owners?
solution: Expected owners = n × p = 250 × 0.30 = 75.

subject: DA
q: A raffle has a 0.003 chance to win. Out of 5,000 tickets, how many winners?
solution: Expected winners = n × p = 5,000 × 0.003 = 15.
trick: 0.003 is 3 in a thousand, so 5,000 tickets gives 5 × 3 = 15.

subject: DA
q: A medical test has a 1% false positive rate. If 1,000 healthy people are tested, how many will falsely test positive?
solution: The false positive rate is the share of healthy people who test positive. So the expected number is 1% of 1,000 = 0.01 × 1,000 = 10. The answer is 10 people.
trick: 1% is one in every hundred, so just do 1,000 ÷ 100 = 10.

subject: DA
q: What is the probability that a randomly chosen integer between 1 and 50 is divisible by 7?
solution: The integers from 1 to 50 are 50 numbers in all. The multiples of 7 are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 and 49, which is 7 numbers. So the probability is 7/50.
trick: 50 ÷ 7 is 7 and a bit, so there are 7 multiples out of 50 numbers: 7/50.

subject: DA
q: Commute times: mean 30 min, SD 5 min. If commute is 25 min, how many SDs from the mean?
solution: z = (value − mean) ÷ SD = (25 − 30) ÷ 5 = −5 ÷ 5 = −1. The minus sign means below the mean, so the commute is 1 SD below. The answer is −1.
trick: 25 is 5 below 30, and one SD is 5, so it is exactly 1 SD below: −1.

subject: DA
q: In hypothesis testing, a sample mean = 52, population mean = 50, standard deviation = 4, n = 16. What is the z-score?
solution: z = (sample mean − population mean) ÷ (SD ÷ √n). The standard error is 4 ÷ √16 = 4 ÷ 4 = 1. So z = (52 − 50) ÷ 1 = 2. The z-score is 2.
trick: √16 = 4 cancels the SD of 4, so the standard error is 1. Then z is just the difference in means: 52 − 50 = 2.

subject: DA
q: How many subsets does a set with 7 elements have?
solution: Each of the 7 elements is either in a subset or out, so there are 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁷ subsets. 2⁷ = 128. The number of subsets is 128.
trick: Double seven times: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. The other options are 2⁶ = 64 and 2⁸ = 256.

subject: DA
q: What is the range of 45, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90?
solution: Range = largest value − smallest value = 90 − 45 = 45. The range is 45.
trick: The list is already in order, so just subtract the two ends: 90 − 45 = 45.

subject: DA
q: For the dataset 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, the third quartile is
solution: There are 7 values, so the median is the 4th value, 10. With the median left out, the top three values are 12, 14 and 16, and the middle of those is 14. So Q3 is 14.
trick: With 7 values, Q3 is the 6th value (the middle of the top three). Count along: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and stop.

subject: DA
q: A class has test scores with a mean of 75 and SD of 5. If a student scores 85, how many SD above the mean is her score?
solution: z = (score − mean) ÷ SD = (85 − 75) ÷ 5 = 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Her score is 2 SD above the mean.
trick: 85 is 10 above 75, and 10 is two lots of 5, so 2 SDs.

subject: DA
q: How many weeks are there in 4 years?
solution: A year has about 52 weeks, so 4 years has 4 × 52 = 208 weeks. As a check, 4 × 365 = 1,460 days and 1,460 ÷ 7 ≈ 208.6, which is 208 full weeks. The answer is 208 weeks.
trick: 4 × 50 = 200 and 4 × 2 = 8, so 208. The other options are far off.

subject: DA
q: The whiskers in a boxplot typically extend to
solution: In a basic boxplot the box runs from Q1 to Q3, and the whiskers reach out from the box to the smallest and largest values. Q1 and Q3 are the ends of the box, not the whiskers, and mean ± SD is not drawn at all. If outliers are plotted separately, the whiskers stop at the most extreme values that are not outliers. So the answer is Minimum and maximum values.
trick: Q1 and Q3 are the box edges and a boxplot never uses mean ± SD, so only the minimum and maximum are left.

subject: DA
q: Phones A, B have P(good battery)=0.7 and 0.8. If one phone is chosen at random, what is P(good)?
solution: Each phone is chosen with probability 1/2. P(good) = 1/2 × 0.7 + 1/2 × 0.8 = 0.35 + 0.40 = 0.75. The probability is 0.75.
trick: Equal chances means take the average of 0.7 and 0.8, which is halfway between them: 0.75.

subject: DA
q: What is the simple interest on ₦5,000 at 8% per annum for 5 years?
solution: Simple interest = P × R × T ÷ 100 = 5,000 × 8 × 5 ÷ 100 = ₦2,000. The simple interest is ₦2,000.
trick: 8% a year for 5 years is 40% of the principal, and 40% of 5,000 is 2,000.

subject: DA
q: Calculate the percentage of 12 girls in a class of 40 students.
solution: Percentage = part ÷ whole × 100 = 12 ÷ 40 × 100 = 0.3 × 100 = 30%. So 30% of the class are girls.
trick: 10% of 40 is 4, and 12 is three lots of 4, so 30%.

subject: DA
q: There are 20 points in a plane. How many triangles can be formed by these points if 5 are collinear?
solution: Any 3 of the 20 points make a triangle, unless all 3 come from the 5 collinear points. The number of triples is C(20, 3) = 20 × 19 × 18 ÷ 6 = 1,140. The 5 collinear points give C(5, 3) = 10 triples that are not triangles. So the number of triangles is 1,140 − 10 = 1,130.
trick: 20 × 19 × 3 = 1,140, then take away 10 to get 1,130. The answer cannot be above 1,140, which rules out 3,310 and 1,210.

subject: DA
q: The response times (in seconds) for a website are 5, 8, 4, 9 and 6. What is the median response time?
solution: Put the times in order: 4, 5, 6, 8, 9. There are 5 values, so the median is the middle one, the 3rd, which is 6. The median response time is 6 seconds.
trick: Sort first, because the middle of the unsorted list is 4. The 3rd smallest is 6.

subject: DA
q: Two dice rolled. Given at least one die shows 4, what is P(the sum is 8)?
solution: There are 36 outcomes, and 25 have no 4, so 36 − 25 = 11 outcomes have at least one 4. Of these, only (4, 4) has a sum of 8. So the probability is 1/11.
trick: Outcomes with a 4: 6 + 6 − 1 = 11. Only the double 4 makes 8, so 1 out of 11.

subject: DA
q: If the quartile deviation is 4, what is the interquartile range?
solution: Quartile deviation = (Q3 − Q1) ÷ 2, which is half the interquartile range. So the IQR = 2 × 4 = 8. The interquartile range is 8.
trick: Quartile deviation is half the IQR, so just double it: 4 × 2 = 8.

q: The number of permutations of 7 objects taken 3 at a time is
solution: Permutations of n objects taken r at a time: P(n, r) = n! ÷ (n − r)!. So P(7, 3) = 7! ÷ 4! = 7 × 6 × 5 = 210. The number of permutations is 210.
trick: Multiply three numbers counting down from 7: 7 × 6 × 5 = 42 × 5 = 210. The other options are 7! = 5,040 and the combinations C(7, 3) = 35.

subject: DA
q: All values in a dataset equal 15. What is the standard deviation?
solution: The standard deviation measures how far the values spread from the mean. If every value is 15, the mean is 15 and every deviation from it is 0. So the variance and the standard deviation are both 0. The answer is 0.
trick: No spread at all means 0. Every value equals the mean, so there is nothing to measure.

subject: DA
q: Which of the following is classified as an unknown or exact value that represents the whole population?
solution: A parameter is a fixed value that describes a whole population, and it is usually unknown. A statistic describes a sample, an estimator is a rule that uses sample data to estimate a parameter, and a predictor is an input variable in a model. So the answer is Parameter.
trick: Parameter goes with Population (both start with P), while a statistic goes with a sample.

subject: DA
q: Three independent events, each with p=0.1. What is the Probability that at least one occurs?
solution: P(at least one) = 1 − P(none). P(none) = 0.9 × 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.729. So P(at least one) = 1 − 0.729 = 0.271.
trick: Use the opposite: 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81, then 0.81 × 0.9 = 0.729, and 1 − 0.729 = 0.271. It cannot be more than 3 × 0.1 = 0.3, so 0.334 is out.

subject: DA
q: If a histogram has a long left tail, which statement is correct?
accept: mean is less than the median
solution: A long left tail means the distribution is negatively skewed. The few very small values pull the mean down towards the tail, while the median stays near the bulk of the data. So the mean is below the median: Mean < Median.
trick: The mean is dragged towards the long tail. The tail is on the left, so the mean sits to the left of the median: mean < median.

subject: DA
q: What is the range of student startup funding rounds ($K): 150, 220, 180, 300, 250, 190?
solution: Range = highest − lowest = 300 − 150 = 150. The range is $150K.
trick: Spot the biggest (300) and the smallest (150) and subtract. The order of the list does not matter.

subject: DA
q: From a standard 52-card deck, what is the probability of drawing an ace or a heart?
solution: There are 4 aces and 13 hearts, but the ace of hearts is counted in both. So there are 4 + 13 − 1 = 16 cards that are an ace or a heart. P = 16/52 = 4/13.
trick: 16 cards out of 52. Divide top and bottom by 4: 4/13.

subject: DA
q: A farmer collects the number of eggs per day from her hens: 12, 15, 10, 20, 30 and 25. What is the median number of eggs?
solution: Put the numbers in order: 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30. There are 6 values, so the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th: (15 + 20) ÷ 2 = 17.5. The median is 17.5 eggs.
trick: With an even count, sort and take the middle pair, 15 and 20, then go halfway: 17.5.

subject: DA
q: In how many ways can 12 identical balls be placed into 5 distinct boxes if each box has at least one ball?
solution: Put 1 ball in each box first, which leaves 12 − 5 = 7 balls to place freely in 5 boxes. By stars and bars the count is C(7 + 5 − 1, 5 − 1) = C(11, 4) = 11 × 10 × 9 × 8 ÷ 24 = 330. The answer is 330.
trick: Use C(11, 4) and cancel early: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, 9 ÷ 3 = 3, 10 ÷ 2 = 5, leaving 11 × 5 × 3 × 2 = 330. The 1,820 option is for boxes that may be empty, so it is out.

subject: DA
q: If covariance is 40 and correlation is 0.8, with X's standard deviation 5, what is the standard deviation?
solution: Correlation r = covariance ÷ (σX × σY), so σX × σY = 40 ÷ 0.8 = 50. The question means the standard deviation of Y, because X's is already given as 5. So σY = 50 ÷ 5 = 10.
trick: 40 ÷ 0.8 is 400 ÷ 8 = 50, which is the product of the two standard deviations. Then 50 ÷ 5 = 10.

subject: DA
q: The range of a dataset is 24, and the highest value is 42. What is the lowest?
solution: Range = highest − lowest, so lowest = highest − range = 42 − 24 = 18.
trick: Subtract in two steps: 42 − 20 = 22, then 22 − 4 = 18.

subject: DA
q: A binomial distribution has n = 400 trials and p = 0.5 success probability. Calculate the standard deviation.
solution: For a binomial distribution, standard deviation = √(npq). Here n = 400, p = 0.5 and q = 0.5, so √(400 × 0.5 × 0.5) = √100 = 10.
trick: When p = 0.5, npq = n ÷ 4, so the standard deviation is √n ÷ 2. √400 = 20, and half of 20 is 10. The option 20 forgets to halve.

subject: DA
q: The interquartile range of exam scores is 10. If the first quartile is 20, what is the third quartile?
solution: Interquartile range = Q3 − Q1, so Q3 = Q1 + IQR = 20 + 10 = 30.
trick: Q3 is just Q1 plus the IQR: 20 + 10 = 30.

subject: DA
q: A pie chart's largest sector is 144 degrees. What percentage of the total does it represent?
solution: A full circle is 360°, so the share is 144 ÷ 360 × 100% = 40%.
trick: Every 36° is 10% of the circle, and 144 ÷ 36 = 4, so the sector is 40%.

subject: DA
q: A dataset has a standard deviation of 5. If each value is increased by 10, what is the new standard deviation?
solution: Standard deviation measures how far values sit from the mean. Adding 10 to every value moves the mean up by 10 as well, so every distance from the mean stays the same. The standard deviation is still 5.
trick: Adding the same number to every value slides the data along without changing its spread, so it stays 5. Only multiplying or dividing would change it.

subject: DA
q: If 60% own cars, 40% bikes, and 25% both, what percent own neither?
solution: Own a car or a bike = 60 + 40 − 25 = 75%, because the 25% who own both were counted twice. Neither = 100% − 75% = 25%, which is 0.25 as a fraction.
trick: 60 + 40 = 100, so the group who own neither is the same size as the group who own both: 25%.

subject: DA
q: Test score frequencies: 10 scored 50, 15 scored 60, 5 scored 70. Find the cumulative frequency ≤60.
solution: Cumulative frequency up to 60 counts everyone who scored 60 or less. That is the 10 who scored 50 plus the 15 who scored 60, so 10 + 15 = 25 students.
trick: Add the frequencies up to 60 and ignore the 70s: 10 + 15 = 25.

subject: DA
q: From a bar chart with maximum height = 25 and minimum height = 5, find the range.
solution: Range = maximum − minimum = 25 − 5 = 20.
trick: Highest bar minus lowest bar: 25 − 5 = 20.

subject: DA
q: If n = 50 and p = 0.7, what is the variance?
solution: Binomial variance = npq = np(1 − p). Here that is 50 × 0.7 × 0.3 = 50 × 0.21 = 10.5.
trick: A binomial variance can never exceed n ÷ 4 = 12.5, because pq is at most 0.25. That rules out 35 and 65 and leaves 10.5.

subject: DA
q: If a dataset follows a normal distribution with mean 50, what is its symmetry point?
solution: A normal distribution is symmetric about its mean, and its mean, median and mode all sit at the same centre. So the symmetry point is the mean, 50.
trick: The bell curve mirrors itself about its mean, so the answer is the mean you were given: 50.

subject: DA
q: A binomial experiment has n = 256, p = 0.5. What is the standard deviation?
solution: Standard deviation = √(npq) = √(256 × 0.5 × 0.5) = √64 = 8.
trick: When p = 0.5, the standard deviation is √n ÷ 2. √256 = 16, and half of 16 is 8. The option 16 forgets to halve.

subject: DA
q: A dataset's range is 24, and its maximum is 42. What is the midrange?
solution: Lowest = highest − range = 42 − 24 = 18. Midrange = (highest + lowest) ÷ 2 = (42 + 18) ÷ 2 = 30.
trick: Midrange is the maximum minus half the range: 42 − 12 = 30.

subject: DA
q: A dataset has values: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. What is the mean absolute deviation?
solution: The mean is (10 + 20 + 30 + 40 + 50) ÷ 5 = 30. The distances from the mean are 20, 10, 0, 10 and 20, which add up to 60. So the mean absolute deviation is 60 ÷ 5 = 12.
